subject: business-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Operations management is mainly concerned with:
options: Producing goods and services by converting inputs into outputs
questions.explain: Operations turns inputs (resources) into outputs (goods/services), adding value.

questions.q: Job production means:
questions.explain: Job production makes single, bespoke items (e.g. a tailored suit).

questions.q: Flow (mass) production involves:
options: Continuous production of large volumes of standardised goods
questions.explain: Flow production continuously makes large quantities of identical products.

questions.q: A bakery producing loaves in groups by type, switching between products, uses:
questions.explain: Batch production makes groups of identical items before switching to another batch.

questions.q: For a high-street retailer, a key location factor is:
questions.explain: Retailers prioritise being close to customers; manufacturers may prioritise costs or suppliers.

questions.q: Reshoring means:
options: Bringing production back to the home country
questions.explain: Reshoring returns previously offshored production to the domestic country.

questions.q: Break-even output is calculated as fixed costs divided by:
questions.explain: Break-even quantity = fixed costs / contribution per unit.

questions.q: Fixed costs are £4,000 and contribution per unit is £8. The break-even output is:
questions.explain: 4,000 / 8 = 500 units to break even.

questions.q: The margin of safety is:
questions.explain: Margin of safety shows how far sales can fall before a loss is made.

questions.q: At the break-even point:
options: Total revenue equals total costs (no profit or loss)
questions.explain: Break-even is where total revenue exactly covers total costs.

questions.q: Adding value in operations means:
options: Increasing the worth of inputs through the production process
questions.explain: Operations add value when outputs are worth more than the inputs used.

questions.q: Operations objectives commonly include cost, quality, speed and:
questions.explain: Key operations objectives are cost, quality, speed, dependability and flexibility.

questions.q: Sustainable operations aim to:
options: Reduce environmental impact and meet needs without harming future generations
questions.explain: Sustainability balances current production with long-term environmental responsibility.

questions.q: Cellular production organises production into:
options: Teams (cells) each responsible for a part of the process
questions.explain: Cellular production groups work into cells/teams, which can improve motivation and flexibility.

questions.q: A capital-intensive production method relies mainly on:
options: Machinery and technology rather than labour
questions.explain: Capital-intensive methods use more machinery; labour-intensive methods use more workers.

questions.q: A firm making thousands of identical bottles per hour most likely uses:
questions.explain: High-volume standardised output suits continuous flow (mass) production.

questions.q: For a heavy-manufacturing firm, an important location factor is:
options: Proximity to raw materials and low transport costs
questions.explain: Bulk-reducing manufacturers often locate near raw materials to cut transport costs.

questions.q: Offshoring means relocating operations:
questions.explain: Offshoring moves operations abroad, often to reduce costs.

questions.q: Contribution per unit equals selling price per unit minus:
questions.explain: Contribution per unit = price − variable cost per unit.

questions.q: A key limitation of break-even analysis is that it assumes:
options: All output produced is sold, and price and costs stay constant
questions.explain: Break-even assumes all output is sold at a constant price with constant costs — often unrealistic.

specSource: IB Diploma Business Management guide (first assessment 2024); Unit 5 — Operations management
